adjudicator: phase4-adjudicator-A (Claude, evidence-led; source-only binding, then visibility)

records.clause: queued but not yet started
records.claimQuote: a deploy or a crash loses any job
records.rationale: Narrows which jobs are lost; the takeaway (the current pool loses jobs) stands. Set.

records.clause: Three VMs plus upgrades and on-call
records.rationale: It explains what the cost is made of and limits nothing. Kept as a visible not_a_condition decision.

records.clause: Uses spare capacity on the existing primary
records.claimQuote: Database job table | $0 extra
records.rationale: R3: '$0 extra' is weighed against load on the primary, which the source calls the main month-end risk (u34). Without the clause, Option C looks free.

records.clause: assumes current volume
records.claimQuote: Managed cloud queue | $310
records.rationale: R2: the figure feeds the cost criterion and the must-have is 3x volume. Uses Y's minimal span, which X's full sentence contains.

records.clause: At three times today's volume it would be roughly $900 a month
records.claimQuote: Managed cloud queue | $310
records.rationale: The projected cost at the must-have volume can reverse the cost comparison. The row's 'grows with volume' does not make the $900 at 3x figure recognisable.

records.clause: until the cluster needs a fourth machine
records.claimQuote: the broker's cost would stay flat
records.rationale: The flat-cost claim is used directly in the 3x-volume cost comparison against $900. Without the bound, a reader would take B's cost as fixed at any volume, and could choose wrongly on the 30% cost criterion. Claim.

records.clause: an option that fails either is out regardless of its score
records.claimQuote: The remaining criteria are weighted for scoring
records.rationale: Without the gate, a high-scoring option that fails a must-have could be chosen.

records.clause: Portability away from our cloud provider: 10%
records.rationale: A criterion weight; limits no claim.

records.clause: the service delivers each message at least once
records.claimQuote: Option A needs almost no operational work
records.rationale: A real limit on A (duplicate delivery), introduced by 'The catch'. But the action-relevant limit that decides the trade-off is the idempotency requirement (k10). The delivery semantics are a cause the notes must contain, without changing the takeaway on their own: set. Found by X only; accepted with a different verdict.

records.clause: every job handler must be made idempotent before we switch
records.claimQuote: Option A needs almost no operational work
records.rationale: R3: the source presents A's benefit as weighed against this catch.

records.clause: today only the email handler is
records.claimQuote: Option A needs almost no operational work
records.readingA: claim: the current status shows how much work stands between A and the switch (all but one handler), so a reader without it would underestimate A's cost and readiness.
records.readingB: set: the requirement 'every job handler must be made idempotent' (k10) already conveys the work; the current status is colour on that requirement.
records.decidingQuestion: Does the source use the current idempotency status to weigh Option A's effort or readiness against B and C, or only as background to the requirement in u27/u44?
records.rationale: The source does not settle it: the status sits inside 'the catch', but no later sentence uses it in a comparison.

records.clause: It also ties us to one provider's API
records.claimQuote: Option A needs almost no operational work
records.rationale: R3: a secondary cost (portability is weighted at 10%).

records.clause: local development needs an emulator that does not support dead-lettering
records.claimQuote: failed messages move to a dead-letter queue automatically
records.rationale: The automatic DLQ claim is false in local development. Only u2_n1 states the DLQ claim.

records.clause: the 12 hours a month is an estimate, not a measurement
records.claimQuote: Self-hosted broker | $540 | about 12 hours
records.rationale: R2: the figure feeds the 40% operational-effort criterion and the source explicitly warns about its reliability.

records.clause: Upgrades need a maintenance window.
records.claimQuote: Option B gives us priority queues and delayed delivery
records.rationale: R3: a secondary operational cost.

records.clause: only covers jobs created inside the billing database transaction
records.claimQuote: a job can never be lost between the commit and the enqueue
records.rationale: 'never be lost' is false outside the transaction. u2_a1's 'for billing-related jobs' conveys this scope.

records.clause: jobs enqueued by the reporting service, which has its own database, would not get it
records.claimQuote: a job can never be lost between the commit and the enqueue
records.rationale: Names the concrete excluded producer. u2_a1 does not make the reporting-service exclusion recognisable.

records.clause: Polling also adds read load to the primary database, which is the main risk at month-end
records.claimQuote: Database job table | $0 extra
records.rationale: Both claim (R3: the source calls it the main risk). Links differ. R4: the transactional guarantee in u32 is not falsified by read load; the '$0 extra' cost claim is what misleads. 'which is the main risk at month-end' qualifies the same clause and is not split.

records.clause: It sustained 1,200 jobs per minute with a p95 claim latency of 18 ms.
records.rationale: A result statement; limited by u38, limits nothing itself.

records.clause: We did not test 1,800 jobs per minute
records.claimQuote: It sustained 1,200 jobs per minute with a p95 claim latency of 18 ms.
records.rationale: R2: explicit reliability warning on evidence for a must-have.

records.clause: the staging copy is about a quarter of production size, so these results may not carry over
records.claimQuote: It sustained 1,200 jobs per minute with a p95 claim latency of 18 ms.
records.rationale: R2: explicit reliability warning.

records.clause: We have not load-tested Options A or B.
records.claimQuote: the provider handles storage, scaling and redelivery
records.rationale: X asked whether any source claim treats A's throughput as established. u7 does: 'the provider handles ... scaling'. A reader taking that as verified would pass A on the 1,800/min must-have. So R2 gives claim, linked to u7, the most specific claim (R4). B has no throughput claim, so for B the clause limits nothing further.

records.clause: but that is the provider's figure, not ours
records.claimQuote: The provider documents throughput far above our peak for Option A
records.rationale: R2: an explicit provenance hedge on decision evidence.

records.clause: until Option C has been measured at 1,800 jobs per minute on a production-sized database
records.claimQuote: The decision is deferred
records.rationale: The unblocking condition. u3_n1 and u3_a1 omit the 1,800/min threshold, so any measurement would seem to settle it; the limit is not recognisable there. The u3_n1->u3_n6 'deferred until' arrow reaches only the 'Option C' shape, not a carrier, and chains do not count.

records.clause: every job handler made idempotent
records.claimQuote: Option A needs almost no operational work
records.rationale: The open requirement restated in its own unit; separate from k10.

records.clause: a named owner for broker on-call and upgrades
records.claimQuote: Option B gives us priority queues and delayed delivery
records.rationale: Both claim (R1: choosing B without an owner leaves no on-call). R4: u8 already says 'we install, patch and monitor ourselves', so it is not misled. The benefit claim u29 is, parallel to u44 -> u26 and u46 -> u32.

records.clause: a passing load test at 1,800 jobs per minute
records.claimQuote: Option C writes a job in the same transaction as the billing change that causes it
records.rationale: Open requirement gating Option C's benefit claim.

rejected.reason: Ordinary approximation, used the same way for all three effort figures (about 2/12/4 hours). It does not limit or hedge the takeaway. The substantive hedge on the 12-hour figure is u30 (k14).

notes: Arrow labels: g3->g2 'defers decision on' is a dependency label, so cards in g2 are linked to carriers in g3 (k26, k27). g2->g5 'cost details', g2->g6 'tested by' and g2->g1 'evaluated by' are not limiting or dependency labels, so they link nothing (k14, k18, k22). The u4_n3->u4_a1 and u2_n1->u2_fs1 card-to-card arrows give 'linked'. The u5_n2 chart counts as a claim card for the cost and effort figures. Citations ignored.
